'''Scott:''' {{legend0|#51C2C2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#2AACAC|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[David Scott (Georgia politician)|David Scott]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Everton Blair]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Georgia}} The '''2026 Georgia's 13th congressional district special election''' was held on July 28, 2026, to elect the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] for {{ushr|GA|13}}. The special election was triggered following the death of incumbent Democratic representative [[David Scott (Georgia politician)|David Scott]] on April 22, 2026. As no candidate received a majority of the vote, a runoff was held on August 25 between Democrats Marcye Scott and [[Everton Blair]].{{cite web |last1=Darnell |first1=Tim |title=Qualifying dates set for special election to fill late David Scott’s congressional seat |url=https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/05/05/qualifying-dates-set-special-election-fill-late-david-scotts-congressional-seat/ |website=Atlanta News First |access-date=7 May 2026 |date=May 5, 2026}} ==Background== Incumbent representative [[David Scott (Georgia politician)|David Scott]] died on April 22, 2026, at 80 years old.{{cite web |last1=Mitchell |first1=Tia |title=Georgia U.S. Rep. David Scott has died |url=https://www.ajc.com/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=22 April 2026 |date=April 22, 2026}} First elected in 2002, Scott had served 12 terms, and was running for a 13th at the time of his death.{{cite web |last1=Raby |first1=Dan |title=Rep. David Scott, longtime Georgia lawmaker, dead at 80 |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/rep-david-scott-longtime-georgia-lawmaker-dead-at-80/ |website=CBS News |access-date=22 April 2026 |date=April 22, 2026}} Governor [[Brian Kemp]] was responsible for calling a special election within 10 days of the vacancy to take place no less than 30 days after the special election is called. {{Cite web |title=2024 CODE OF GEORGIA :: Title 21 - ELECTIONS (§§ 21-1-1 — 21-5-76) :: Chapter 2 - ELECTIONS AND PRIMARIES GENERALLY (§§ 21-2-1 — 21-2-604) :: Article 14 - SPECIAL ELECTIONS AND PRIMARIES GENERALLY (§§ 21-2-540 — 21-2-546) :: Section 21-2-543 - Special election for United States congressional representative vacancy |url=https://law.justia.com/codes/georgia/title-21/chapter-2/article-14/section-21-2-543/ |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=Justia Law |language=en}} Per Georgia state law, all candidates will run on one ballot, with a [[Two-round system|runoff election]] scheduled for the top-two candidates if none receive over 50% of the vote.{{cite news |title=Marjorie Taylor Greene resigns. Now what? |first=Tim |last=Darnell |work=[[WANF]] |date=November 21, 2025 |access-date=April 22, 2025 |url=https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2025/11/22/marjorie-taylor-greene-resigns-now-what/}} On May 1, Kemp scheduled the election for July 28, 2026.{{cite web |last1=Darnell |first1=Tim |title=Special election set to fill US Rep. David Scott’s 13th district seat |url=https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/05/01/special-election-set-fill-david-scotts-13th-district-seat/ |website=Atlanta News First |access-date=1 May 2026 |date=May 1, 2026}} As no candidate got a majority, the runoff election was held August 25, 2026.{{cite web |url=https://sos.ga.gov/news/call-special-election-congressional-district-13 |date=May 5,
